annotations.title: Verify an email address before you send

description: Will mail to this address arrive? Checked now at the source: syntax, the domain's own DNS (MX, null MX, no such domain) and its own mail server, asked whether the mailbox exists and whether it accepts every address (catch-all). No message is sent. Flags disposable domains, role accounts (info@, sales@), free providers, likely typos (gmial.com) and the mail provider. Verdict: deliverable, undeliverable, risky or unknown, with the reason. Input: email. $0.02 per call. Returns: email, normalized, local_part, domain, domain_ascii, verdict, reason, syntax_valid, domain_exists, accepts_mail, mx[{host, priority}], mail_provider, mailbox{checked, exists, catch_all, smtp_code, smtp_message, mx_host}, disposable, role_account, free_provider, did_you_mean, disposable_list_as_of, notes[], checked_at.

email.description: One email address, such as jane@example.com.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 language tag (en, ja, ko, pt-BR): the human-readable strings of the result (notes, details, reasons) are translated into this language; data, codes, numbers and URLs are untouched. Default: as produced.

name: hubvibe_email_verify

outputSchema.description: The 200 body of every paid /work call. `result` is the worker's own output (its schema is per route); everything else is the same on every /work route. A receipt for the job is at `receipt_url`.

billing_warning.description: Present only when the charge was recorded with a caveat.

price_usd.description: What this call cost, in USD.

provenance.description: How the result was produced: which providers ran and how long each took.

attempts.description: Provider attempts made, including retries and failovers.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds for the whole job.

steps.description: Every step the job ran, in order.

reason.description: Failure reason, on a failed step.

receipt_url.description: Where to fetch the machine-readable receipt (free, no payment).

accepts_mail.description: The domain has somewhere to deliver mail (MX or address fallback); null when not looked up.

checked_at.description: When this node read the source (UTC). Nothing here is cached.

did_you_mean.description: A likely intended address when the domain looks like a typo of a common provider.

disposable.description: The domain is a known throwaway-mail domain.

disposable_list_as_of.description: Date of the disposable-domain list used.

domain_ascii.description: The domain in ASCII (punycode for internationalised names); null when invalid.

domain_exists.description: The domain exists in DNS; null when not looked up.

free_provider.description: A free consumer mail provider (gmail.com, outlook.com...).

mail_provider.description: Who runs the domain's mail (google, microsoft, yahoo, zoho, proton, amazon_ses...); null when not recognised.

catch_all.description: The server also accepted a random address on the domain; null when not tested.

checked.description: The mail server gave a yes-or-no answer about the mailbox.

exists.description: The mailbox exists; null when it could not be proved.

smtp_code.description: The server's reply code to the mailbox question.

mx.description: The domain's mail servers, in the order mail tries them.

normalized.description: Local part with the domain lower-cased and punycoded; null when the syntax is invalid.

examples: Role address: it usually reaches a team or a shared inbox, not one person.

reason.description: Why the verdict is what it is.

role_account.description: The local part is a role (info, sales, support...), not a person.

verdict.description: deliverable: the mail server confirmed the mailbox. undeliverable: bad syntax, no such domain, no mail server, or no such mailbox. risky: disposable domain or a server that accepts every address. unknown: the server would not say.

status.description: Present only on a delivered result.

worker.description: Catalog name of the worker that ran.

outputSchema.title: email.verify response

title: Verify an email address before you send
